classification.difficultyReason: Finds probabilities within a family and then combines outcomes across five families, with modelling assumptions.

content.prompt: Five families have three children each. For parts a and b, find the probability correct to three decimal places.

children.label: a
children.prompt: At least one of these families has three boys.

answer.worked:
For one family, $P(\text{three boys})=(\frac12)^3=\frac18$.
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{at least one family has three boys})&=1-\left(\frac78\right)^5\\&\approx0.487.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Each family has more boys than girls.

answer.worked:
For one family, let $Y\sim\operatorname{Bin}(3,\frac12)$ count boys.
$$\begin{aligned}P(Y\ge2)&=\binom32\left(\frac12\right)^3+\left(\frac12\right)^3\\&=\frac48=\frac12.\end{aligned}$$
$$\begin{aligned}P(\text{all five families have more boys than girls})&=\left(\frac12\right)^5\\&=\frac1{32}\\&\approx0.031.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: What assumptions have been made in arriving at your answers?

answer.short: Boys and girls are equally likely, births are independent, and every child is classified as a boy or a girl.
answer.worked: Assume each child has probability $\frac12$ of being a boy and $\frac12$ of being a girl, every child is classified as a boy or a girl, and births are independent within and between families.
